title: RWB-S8-E2009-APP: a P9 Reporting story is placed in rwb-deviation with one C row and an empty build row, and the seven owner reads, the matrix edge and the platform prerequisites are unpublished
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2, R7.3 and R9; context pack S8 rwb-deviation and the connection matrix on Architecture v5 slide 13; split plan story line RWB-S8-E2009-APP; legacy RWB-E2-009 metadata, sections 3, 4 and 12
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies); Sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 12.1, 12.2, 12.8 and 13
description: (1) The legacy story names module P9 Reporting and its facts are rwb-reporting's, while the plan places this APP slice in rwb-deviation (S8) with C RWB-P9-E2009-CON and no H row, so two services appear to serve the same steering data set. (2) The connection matrix gives S8 no REST call to P9 and gives P9 no subscription to S8, so the one C row has no edge in the matrix. (3) The story reads seven operations of five owners (the reporting measure set, the case facts and case-list count, the treatment facts, the decision facts, the notice facts, the agent run facts and the hold notification) and no source publishes an operation name for any of them; only the reporting read is covered by the C row. (4) The pattern set carries DP03, DP07, DP10, DP15 and DP19, and the DP table makes each add an H dependency on a platform contract story (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, E1043, E1071, E1044 and N001), yet the plan's build row is empty.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-009 metadata row Module P9 Reporting, section 12 endpoints on /api/recovery/v1/reports/measures and the six published interfaces called; split plan slice RWB-S8-E2009-APP with H [] and C [RWB-P9-E2009-CON]; Architecture v5 slide 13 row S8 Deviation (P3 E, P1 R E, P10 T E; no R to P9) and row P9 Reporting (no E at S8); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP rows 03, 07, 10, 15 and 19; context pack S8 ownership rows (REST operations provided 2, both case writes; tables 1; jobs 0)
proposed: Keep the plan's service, lane, C row and empty H row as they stand; record the slice as the secondary serving of the steering data set in S8, with the canonical measure build, the measure tables, the baseline and the Power BI read model staying with rwb-reporting; publish the seven consumed operation names with their owners before the contract is tagged, and confirm the load-time edge with the P9 and S8 owners

title: RWB-S8-E2009-APP: DP-17 removes the data lake, so the INT-19 extract and the Power BI data set of the story have no target owner and no replacement path in this service
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17 and R5.5 DP-19; context pack S8 (no data lake, rwb-reporting builds its read model from events); legacy RWB-E2-009 sections 2, 4 and 12
description: The legacy story publishes an INT-19 extract for the 07:30 Power BI refresh and shows the same values on SCR-37 and in Power BI from one measure_snapshot set. Arch v5 removes the data lake and INT-19/INT-20, rwb-reporting builds its read model from events, and the connection matrix gives S8 no file and no lake link, so the extract has no owner and no target in this slice. The freshness stamp on the answer is kept and serves the screen, and the Power BI path is left to the reporting service's own story.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-009 sections 2, 4 (step 4, the INT-19 extract with the freshness stamp; step 5, the Power BI refresh at 07:30) and section 12; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17 (data lake, INT-19, INT-20 removed; gap if the story needs lake data) and DP-19; context pack S8 (no data lake; reporting from events)
proposed: Drop the INT-19 extract from this slice, keep the freshness stamp on the answer for the 07:30 screen refresh, and move the Power BI data set to the rwb-reporting read model built from events; confirm the replacement path with the reporting owner before the wave 2 entry check

title: RWB-S8-E2009-APP: the plan assigns the slice no legacy acceptance criterion while it keeps ten legacy test cases, and the legacy criteria lose their owned ids
source: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s7 and s16, R7.3 and R9; split plan story line RWB-S8-E2009-APP (acs empty, tcs_legacy 10); legacy RWB-E2-009 sections 7 and 16
description: The story line gives acs as an empty list and tcs_legacy as the ten legacy cases of RWB-E2-009, so no legacy AC id is owned by this slice, although the legacy story holds nine criteria and TC-E2-009-01 to TC-E2-009-09 trace to them one to one and TC-E2-009-10 is an access test with no AC. The template forbids a scenario without an origin tag and forbids inventing business values, so the nine criteria are restated as new under D-RCV-60 with the legacy values kept word for word, and the ten test cases keep their legacy ids and their covers mapping.
evidence: Split plan slice RWB-S8-E2009-APP acs [] and tcs_legacy 10; legacy RWB-E2-009 section 7 (AC1 to AC9) and section 16 (TC-E2-009-01 to TC-E2-009-10, TC-10 level Access with no AC); Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s7 origin tag rule and R9 placeholder rule
proposed: Keep acs empty in the fragment and restate AC1 to AC9 as new (D-RCV-60) with the legacy values; carry TC-E2-009-01 to TC-E2-009-10 unchanged, map TC-E2-009-10 to the access refusal, and record the mapping in section 18 so the legacy criteria remain traceable to their legacy ids

title: RWB-S8-E2009-APP: the schedule time, the dimension format, the two added Measure fields and the alert recipients have no published values for the deviation serving
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5, R5.7 and R9; split plan story line RWB-S8-E2009-APP; legacy RWB-E2-009 sections 4, 12, 13, 14 and 15; context pack S8 rwb-deviation
description: (1) The legacy story runs JOB-15 at 01:30 and the DP-10 row moves it to a Temporal Schedule, but no source publishes the schedule id, its calendar, its catch-up policy or its rerun input. (2) The legacy story records that the Measure schema has no dimension or baseline field and adds them in an additions file; no source publishes the final field names or the dimension code format, which the story keeps as agent:case-intake:1.2.0. (3) The hold alert names two roles and no channel; the notification is taken to be rwb-comms' contract with a fake. (4) The product, route and measure lists the filters offer have no published reference-data row set.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-009 sections 4 (JOB-15 at 01:30), 12 (Measure has no dimension or baseline field; additions file), 13 (configuration and reference data), 14 (MSG-P9-002 alert) and 15 (SCR-37 states); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07 and DP-10, R5.7 (Day 1), R9; context pack S8 (jobs 0; queue rwb-deviation); Architecture v5 slide 13
area: Schedule, message shape and reference data
proposed: Publish the schedule id, calendar, catch-up policy and rerun input with the workflow kit owner; publish the two Measure fields and the dimension format with the reporting owner; confirm the notification channel and the two recipients with rwb-comms; and read the three filter lists as reference data of rwb-case at their version
